title: [0.17.0+] backup command reports "Access is denied" errors on Windows
body:

Output of `restic version`
--------------------------
0.17.0+


What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------
Another local drive on Windows


Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------
```Powershell
restic backup "F:\library" --exclude "F:\library\thumbs" --exclude "F:\library\encoded-video"
```


<!--
This section should include at least:

 * A description of the problem you are having with restic.

 * The complete command line and any environment variables you used to
   configure restic's backend access. Make sure to replace sensitive values!

 * The output of the commands, what restic prints gives may give us much
   information to diagnose the problem!

 * The more time you spend describing an easy way to reproduce the behavior (if
   this is possible), the easier it is for the project developers to fix it!
-->


Expected behavior
-----------------
No error.

<!--
Describe what you'd like restic to do differently.
-->

Actual behavior
---------------
Show following errors on every dirs and files:
```
error: incomplete metadata for F:\library\database-backup: get named security info failed with: Access is denied.
```


<!--
In this section, please try to concentrate on observations, so only describe
what you observed directly.
-->

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------
Tested with 0.16.5 and got no errors.

<!--
Did something noteworthy happen on your system, Internet connection, backend services, etc?
-->

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Can you please try to reproduce the problem with the latest restic 0.17.2 which you can download at https://github.com/restic/restic/releases ?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Updated to 0.17.2, still got same error.

The folder to backup was the library of [immich app](https://github.com/immich-app/immich), which I was running with docker on Windows. The dirs are mapped to the ones inside the docker container. I'm not sure if the access error is related to this.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> The working directory is `F:\`.
> [...]
> The volume mappings were not changed at all from day one and work fine with restic 0.16.5

@reporter That is only a description of how you've configured immich. But that doesn't describe the connection between `F:\` and `./library`. `./library` is clearly a unix path, how does that path end up at `F:\` in Windows? Is that some WSL mount or Docker desktop or something else?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> how does that path end up at F:\ in Windows?

I am using docker desktop based on WSL. Just checked in WSL, Windows drives are automatically mounted at `/mnt/` path. So `F:\` in Windows is `/mnt/f` in WSL.

> `./library` is clearly a unix path

Yes. Its absolute path in WSL is `/mnt/f/library`, which is a mount point of `F:\library` in Windows.

So the mappings in my case is like:

|Windows Path|WSL Path|Container Path|
|---|---|---|
|`F:\library`|`/mnt/f/library`|`/usr/src/app/upload`|



As for restic backup, WSL is irrelative. I'm directly backing up the folder `F:\library` to the target repo.
